title: Safety-first deployment wizard — operator checklist & wireframe notes
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working draft for a safety-first staged deployment wizard in the Console. Goal: give operators a compact, risk-aware flow for canaries, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies that minimizes cognitive load and prevents accidental wide releases. Focus is on default safe choices, clear guardrails, and fast recovery primitives.

Primary personas:
- Platform operator (SRE/infra platform) — needs safety, observability hooks, quick rollback paths.
- Product engineer (owner of a feature) — wants predictable ramp and experiment metrics.
- Support/Oncall — needs clear runbooks surfaced and one-click containment.

High-level UX goals:
- Make safe options the default (e.g., conservative initial traffic, auto-monitor windows enabled).
- Surface critical health signals (latency P90, error rate, quality regressions) inline during creation.
- Reduce friction for common operator actions: pause, rollback, fast-forward, modify weight.
- Make fallback policies explicit and testable before deployment.
- Keep the wizard short (3–5 steps) with in-line explanations and example defaults.

Suggested wizard steps (3-step primary flow + optional advanced):
1) Deployment summary (tile view)
   - Inputs: model/version, route, baseline variant, candidate variant(s).
   - Quick validations: model compatibility, required resources, region constraints.
   - Safety defaults (read-only toggles): "Start with 1% traffic for 30m", "Enable auto-fallback: enabled".
   - Microcopy hint: "We’ll hold traffic at 1% and monitor health for 30 minutes. You can change this after creation."

2) Rules & Guards (the safety core)
   - Traffic schedule: initial weight, step increments, max weight, step interval (mins). Defaults: 1%, +5% every 20m, max 50% unless operator explicitly sets otherwise.
   - Health checks: required signals to progress (p50/p95 latency, error rate, model quality delta). Provide examples and suggested thresholds.
   - Fallback policy selection: dropdown with presets (Immediate failover, Gradual rollback, Hold-and-alert). Descriptions + tradeoffs.
   - Manual override switch: "Allow manual override during ramp" (off by default).
   - Wireframe note: for each rule, show inline "What happens if this fires" tooltip.

3) Observability & Notifications
   - Choose probes: latency, errors, custom eval metric (prompt set). Default probe set preselected for model generation routes.
   - Alerting targets: Slack channel, PagerDuty service, and runbook link field.
   - Preview dashboard link (opens in a side-panel) that shows the exact signals used for gating.

Optional advanced panel (collapsible):
   - Traffic slicing rules (by user bucket, route path, region).
   - Canary sampling policy (random vs deterministic hashing).
   - Quota & cost ceilings (optional hard caps).

Wireframe/visual notes (sketch-level):
- Top breadcrumb: "Create staged deployment > Guards > Observability > Review"
- Left column (compact): deployment summary and quick stats. Right column (larger): interactive rule editor with sliders for weights and toast previews of schedule timeline.
- Scheduler preview: small timeline visualization (minute buckets) with annotations when checks run and when fallback might trigger. Use low-contrast colors for default safe-range and bright warning color for threshold breaches.
- Inline simulation: a small control to run a "simulated traffic run" using historical traces to preview how schedule would progress and what checks would fire. (UI: "Simulate using last 24h traffic")

Operator checklist (pre-creation) — quick items displayed as collapsible checklist: 
- [ ] Confirm baseline variant pinned (if needed)
- [ ] Attach runbook URL or pick default
- [ ] Confirm required metrics are available for this route
- [ ] Confirm cost cap if appropriate
- [ ] Choose fallback preset (and read description)

Microcopy examples (short):
- Step header: "Set the safety defaults — you can relax them after the canary proves healthy."
- Fallback preset: "Immediate failover — stop traffic to candidate and route to baseline instantly. Use for critical latency/error failures."
- Tooltip for simulation: "Simulate the ramp using recent traffic to see when gates will check. Simulation is approximate."

Edge cases & decision notes (open questions):
- How to handle multi-model rollouts that change output schema? Suggest enforcing a "schema compatibility" check in Step 1 and block auto-progress if incompatible.
- If observability signals are missing (e.g., customer hasn’t enabled prompt-set evals), show a warning and auto-disable that gate — but surface that the fallback will be less informed.
- Gradual rollback vs. immediate: include a guardrail to prevent accidental full rollbacks if rollback itself might be unsafe for some workloads (e.g., stateful integrations).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Operator can create a staged deployment in 3 steps with default safe values.
- System validates model compatibility and required metrics before starting.
- Simulated preview works with 24h traffic sample and shows potential gate triggers.
- Fallback presets behave as documented and can be executed manually with one click.
- Audit event entries created for all state transitions (start ramp, pause, fallback, rollback).

Backlog / tickets to create (first-pass):
- (JIRA) ROLLOUT-401: Wizard UI skeleton + routing of inputs (est 5d).
- (JIRA) ROLLOUT-402: Rule editor component (sliders + timeline preview) (est 6d).
- (JIRA) ROLLOUT-403: Simulation backend endpoint and sample connector (est 8d).
- (JIRA) ROLLOUT-404: Fallback policy engine + presets (est 7d).
- (JIRA) ROLLOUT-405: Audit log events + runbook linking (est 3d).
- (JIRA) ROLLOUT-406: Observability integration (alerting + dashboard preview) (est 5d).

Accessibility & performance considerations:
- Keep text density low; use progressive disclosure for advanced knobs.
- Timeline visual should be keyboard-navigable and provide text equivalents.
- Avoid large synchronous simulations on the main thread — use async job + spinner.

Quick grooming notes (what to discuss in next session):
- Decide default escalation window for auto-fallback (30m vs 60m) and which metric set is required by default.
- Set guardrail limits for maximum initial exposure (should a policy enforce <=10% by default for unmanaged orgs?).
- Which teams own runbook defaults for alerts? (SRE vs product teams)

Open/To-do (notes to self):
- Add micro-interaction for "pause and snapshot" — when operator pauses the ramp, capture a snapshot of traffic + metrics for debug.
- Prototype a tiny animation for the timeline that shows progression and gating points.
- Validate language with legal/security for auto-fallback behaviors on private deployments.

Quick links / references used while writing: 
- Existing guarded rollout observations in Confluence: CONFLUENCE-12345
- Past incident where auto-fallback would have helped: INC-2024-07 (summary in ticket)

Comments requested from reviewers (please leave inline):
- Is the default schedule too conservative/unusable?
- Are the fallback presets comprehensible? Which additional preset would you want?
- Is simulation useful, or too many false positives?

Bottom line: goal for MVP is to prioritize safety and clarity over configurability. We can add more slicing options and fancier scheduling later, but we must ship an operator-friendly, default-safe flow that reduces the chance of wide regressions.
